facts.quote: Teaching vignette (invented): five H&E slides of sentinel lymph node tissue from one patient, as released in the public CAMELYON17 data set. The data set labels each slide as one node by its largest focus, so call each slide as one node even if it shows more than one profile of nodal tissue. No immunohistochemistry, deeper levels, primary tumour, gross description or clinical history exists for these slides; this vignette is invented for teaching and carries no patient information. Review every node, call each one, and stage the set under CAMELYON17's simplified rules.
facts.basis: Invented for teaching (D13, §15.2): one generic text for all ten cases, labelled "Teaching vignette (invented)"; CAMELYON17 publishes no clinical record (FACTS §0). Its one dataset claim, one slide = one node, is S0.1 in common.facts.json.

facts.quote: Five slides, one node each by the data set's convention. Open every node, call each one, then fill the practice report.
facts.basis: The data set's one-slide-one-node convention (S0.1, common.facts.json); the rest is instruction.

facts.quote: Reference: negative (CAMELYON17 label). Negative nodes carry no annotation, so there is nothing to show.
facts.basis: stages.csv (sha256 1bf47c5c3b20…) row patient_017_node_0.tif = negative (FACTS §0); no negative slide has an annotation XML in CAMELYON17 (FACTS §4.3); D18.

facts.quote: Reference: isolated tumour cells, about 84 µm (longest single annotated outline; CAMELYON17 annotation of 1 polygon, about 0.0024 mm²). Under AJCC breast staging, which CAMELYON17 applies, a node with ITCs only is not counted toward the number of positive nodes.
facts.basis: stages.csv (sha256 1bf47c5c3b20…) row patient_017_node_1.tif = itc; annotations/patient_017_node_1.xml converted to overlays/patient_017_node_1.geojson (layer version 2bf0a484): 1 Tumor polygon(s); largest single polygon Feret 83.6 µm; polygons within 100 µm merged span 83.6 µm (1 cluster(s)); area 0.002417 mm²; at this slide's 0.2431 µm/px (XResolution 4294967295/104408 pixels per cm (RATIONAL, ResolutionUnit 3)); Feret by convex hull, written "about" to two significant figures. The outline is the challenge's annotation extent, not a pathologist's measurement of this case (PE-10; FACTS §4.3, §1.1). The ITC sentence is AJCC 8th edition's rule for breast pN, applied by the challenge (S0.2, PE-1).

facts.quote: Reference pN: pN1 under CAMELYON17's simplified rules (3 nodes with micro- or macrometastasis, at least one of them a macrometastasis; the ITC-only node is not counted as positive, as in AJCC). The largest annotated deposit is in node 3; node 4 is a macrometastasis by label without an annotation, so the case's largest deposit is not compared.
facts.basis: stages.csv (sha256 1bf47c5c3b20…) patient row patient_017.zip = pN1; derivePn of the node labels ['negative', 'itc', 'macro', 'macro', 'micro'] gives pN1 (the rules reproduce stages.csv for 100 of 100 patients, FACTS §4.1, §4.2); counts macro 2, micro 1, ITC 1, positive 3. Largest annotated deposit: node 3 (3157.9 µm); not compared because an unannotated node carries a label of the same or higher rank (GRD-N6).

facts.quote: Node 2 carries isolated tumour cells. Under AJCC breast staging, which CAMELYON17 applies, a node with ITCs only is not counted toward the number of positive nodes, so three positive nodes give pN1, not pN2.
facts.basis: stages.csv: node_1 itc, nodes 2 and 3 macro, node 4 micro, pN1; with ITC counted the set would have four positive nodes (pN2). ITC-only nodes are excluded from the positive-node count by AJCC 8th edition (applied by the challenge; S0.2, PE-1; one of the six ITC-proof patients of FACTS §4.1).

facts.quote: Only nodes 2, 3 and 5 are annotated in CAMELYON17; node 4 is a macrometastasis by label alone, so no location or size can be shown for it, and the case's largest deposit is not compared.
facts.basis: annotations/ holds patient_017_node_1, _2 and _4 only (FACTS §4.3); node_3 is macro in stages.csv; the largest deposit is not compared when an unannotated node may hold it (§6.3, GRD-N6).
